newsitem.title: BRAZIL: AES, ABB compete for Brazil power project.
newsitem.headline: AES, ABB compete for Brazil power project.

text.p: AES Corp of the United States and Swedish-Swiss owned ABB Group have submitted bids on a state thermoelectric power project in southern Brazil, an official said.

A spokeswoman for Rio Grande do Sul state said the firms are competing to build and operate a roughly $230 million plant that would use natural gas imported from Argentina to produce 450 megawatts (MW) of power.
The details of the proposals were not made public but the state will pick a winner by the end of February, she said.
"The company that offers to sell the energy, on a per megawatt basis, most cheaply will win the contract," she said.

The plant, which would consume a maximum 2.5 million cubic meters of gas a day, would be built near the border town of Uruguaiana, she added. Gas would be transported from Argentina via a 273-mile (440-km) gasline and the power produced by the plant would flow into the state's power grid. "The Urugaiana plant would be operating by the end of 1998 or early 1999," the spokeswoman said.
AES has already announced that, if picked, its supplier would be Westinghouse Electric Corp, she said.
